name: ReadModel
summary: Read a constructive amplitude model or an imported CalcHEP Feynman model.

syntaxes.description: Read the numbered model files from a directory.

details: A constructive model is the four-element list {particles, amplitudes, variables, functions}. Its data come from prtclsN.mdl, ampsN.mdl, varsN.mdl and funcN.mdl. Keep this list and pass it to other HEPCAT functions.

When lgrngN.mdl is present and ampsN.mdl is absent, the reader recognizes a CalcHEP model and returns FeynmanModel[particles, vertices, variables, functions]. Bare Feynman vertices are not complete lower-point amplitudes for constructive factorization.
Parameters are inert model-local ModelParameter objects. Reading two models does not assign global symbols such as Me or EE, and one model cannot silently change another model's values.

Use the QED model containing three-point vertices for diagrams. Use a model containing complete four-point amplitudes when factorizing a five-point process, and complete five-point amplitudes when factorizing a six-point process. An amplitude missing from the supplied factorization model is treated as zero.
The reader reports malformed, unavailable or unterminated model tables as failures rather than executing arbitrary expressions from model text.

examples.description: Read the bundled QED three-point model and see its four sections.
Retrieve a mass and its locally resolved numerical value.

name: ReadVariables
summary: Read a model variable table without assigning global parameter values.

syntaxes.description: Return the variable rows in a numbered varsN.mdl file.

details: Each returned row contains {parameter, value, comment}, with parameter represented by ModelParameter[name, scope, "Real"]. The scope separates models that happen to use the same parameter name.
The table requires its final separator. Invalid arithmetic or malformed rows are rejected by the model expression parser.
ReadModel normally calls this reader for you. For numerical calculations, use ModelParameterRules on the complete model so dependent functions and overrides are resolved consistently.

examples.description: Inspect one declared variable.
List the declared names rather than assigning them.

name: ReadFunctions
summary: Read the dependent parameter expressions in a model function table.

syntaxes.description: Return the rows of a funcN.mdl table.

details: Rows retain a model-local parameter, its defining expression and any comment. Reading a dependent parameter is distinct from numerically resolving it.
Supported arithmetic is parsed as inert model data. An external function is retained as ModelFunction rather than called in the Wolfram session.
Use ModelParameterRules[model] to obtain the numerically resolved subset. A cyclic dependency or unsupported external function does not prevent unrelated resolvable parameters from being used.

examples.description: Inspect the QED dependent definitions.
Resolve the complete model locally.

name: ReadParticles
summary: Read particle and antiparticle declarations from a model table.

syntaxes.description: Read the eleven-column prtclsN.mdl table.

details: The columns retain the full name, particle name, antiparticle name, identifier, twice the spin, mass, width, color, auxiliary information and two display names. The list order and particle names are model data, not newly created Wolfram symbols.
Mass parameters are parsed into model-local ModelParameter references. ParticleMass searches both the particle and antiparticle columns.
Diagram generation and automatic identical-particle symmetry use particle identities and twice-spin declarations. Equal masses alone do not identify particles.

examples.description: Read the particle table.
Find the electron mass from the particle declarations.

name: ParticleMass
summary: Look up a particle or antiparticle mass in a particle table.

syntaxes.description: Return the mass declared for a particle name.

details: The second argument is the particle section of a model, normally model[[1]], rather than the entire four-element model.
The lookup recognizes either the particle name or its antiparticle name. It returns the declared symbolic mass, including a ModelParameter when that is what the model contains.
The empty padding name "" has mass 0. An unknown nonempty particle name returns -1. Check for this sentinel when accepting user particle names.

examples.description: Particle and antiparticle have the declared common mass.
examples.input:
qedModel = ReadModel[modelDirectory, 2];
ParticleMass["e", qedModel[[1]]] === ParticleMass["E", qedModel[[1]]]

examples.description: Distinguish model padding from an unknown name.

name: ReadAmplitudes
summary: Read complete constructive amplitudes and their separate overall factors.

syntaxes.description: Read an ampsN.mdl table using the particle declarations for spin and mass information.

details: An amplitude row contains the external particle names, optional empty padding columns, an overall factor and the expression divided by that factor. The last two entries are therefore multiplied to obtain the full stored amplitude.
The reader uses ConvertAmplitude to translate compact bracket notation into typed HEPCAT expressions. It does not automatically invent missing opposite-helicity amplitudes.
The factorization code treats an unlisted lower-point amplitude as zero. Populate the model with the complete lower-point results needed by the intended calculation.
ReadModel normally reads the matching particle and amplitude files together and should be preferred for routine use.

examples.description: Read the QED vertex-amplitude rows explicitly.
Recover the complete expression in one row.

name: ConvertAmplitude
summary: Convert a constructive model row from text into typed spinor notation.

syntaxes.description: Convert the final amplitude string using the row's external particles.
Use an explicit parameter scope for model data.

details: The row has particle-name columns followed by an overall factor and an amplitude string. The return value is the converted final expression; the separate overall factor is not multiplied into it.
Compact angle and square brackets become SpinorChain expressions. Interior digits become momentum insertions; the particle table selects massive "Spin" or massless "Helicity" endpoints.
The converter recognizes x factors, propagator denominators and declared model parameters. For example, s13-Me^2 represents PropDen[Mom[Multiparticle[1,3]], Me] with the model-local mass parameter.
Compact bracket digits are single-digit labels. Use typed SpinorChain, Spinor and Mom expressions when multi-digit external labels or more explicit structures are required.
The current converter uses the restricted model expression parser. ConvertAmplitudeOld is retained for historical compatibility and is not the recommended model reader.

examples.description: Translate a massive angle bracket from a three-point row.
Convert a photon square bracket in a four-point row.

name: ConvertAmplitudeOld
summary: Access the historical string converter retained for compatibility.

syntaxes.description: Use the older string-replacement converter; new code should use ConvertAmplitude.

details: This historical implementation predates the model-local parameter parser. Its original spinor-type setup is no longer active in the function, so it is not a supported replacement for the current row-based converter.
The old implementation uses general string replacement and expression conversion. Do not use it to import arbitrary model text or rely on it for multi-digit labels.
For new work, load an entire model with ReadModel or call ConvertAmplitude with a full row and particle table.

examples.description: A scalar constant is a minimal compatibility example.

name: AddOppositeHelicityAmplitudes
summary: Mechanically add angle-square conjugate rows with reversed massless helicities.

syntaxes.description: Retain each row and add its helicity-reversed bracket partner when applicable.

details: For a row containing particle names ending in .+ or .-, the added row reverses all of those suffixes, interchanges angle and square spinors, and interchanges xFactor with xTildeFactor. The separate factor is retained.

This is a mechanical model-building operation, not a proof of a model's parity properties or coupling conjugation conventions. Verify the resulting amplitude and normalization for the theory being entered.
ReadAmplitudes does not currently call this operation automatically. Explicitly listed helicity amplitudes remain the clearest way to specify a complete model.

examples.description: Inspect the two helicity names in a small row pair.
Inspect the converted square-bracket partner.

name: AppendModelAmplitudes
summary: Append validated text representations of supplied amplitudes to a constructive model file.

syntaxes.description: Append {particles, amplitude} or {particles, factor, amplitudeOverFactor} entries to ampsN.mdl.

details: This function writes amplitudes already obtained by the user. It does not derive them or establish their physical correctness. Run CheckAmplitudes and independent checks before making an amplitude available as factorization input.
Particle and parameter declarations come from the target model. Every new row must round-trip through the model reader before the file is replaced atomically.
The returned association has keys "File", "Added" and "Skipped". Repeating an identical append is a no-op; a conflicting amplitude for an existing particle multiset rejects the batch.
Existing comments and rows are preserved. Reload ReadModel after writing. Use a temporary copy for experiments rather than changing the bundled model in a help example.

name: ModelParameter
summary: Represent and retrieve a parameter belonging to one model.

syntaxes.description: Find a declared parameter by its string name.
Retain a parameter as inert model-local data.

details: Parameters display their model names, such as Me or EE, but are not global Wolfram symbols. Keep the typed parameter in expressions and obtain numerical replacements with ModelParameterRules.
The scope separates declarations belonging to different model data. A string lookup returns Failure when the name is absent or ambiguous; it does not create a new declaration.

The domain "Real" makes Conjugate[parameter] evaluate to parameter. Imported model declarations currently retain this real-parameter convention. Other domains do not receive that automatic conjugation rule.

Use ModelParameterName to inspect the displayed name. Directly constructing a reference is mainly useful for tools that preserve model data; routine physics code should retrieve the reference from its model.

examples.description: Retrieve a declared electron mass.

name: ModelFunction
summary: Retain an external model function call as inert data.

syntaxes.description: Represent an external function belonging to a model.

details: The model expression reader can encounter named functions that are not supported numerical arithmetic. Such a call is stored rather than executed in the caller's session.
StandardForm and TraditionalForm display a familiar function call while retaining the typed head internally. PlainText, TeX and SPINAS preserve its name and arguments for output.
An unsupported function prevents a dependent parameter from resolving numerically. It does not justify executing an arbitrary Wolfram function with the same displayed name.

examples.description: Inspect an inert call without invoking a global function.
Convert the retained call to model-style text.

name: ModelParameterName
summary: Get the string name of a model-local parameter.

syntaxes.description: Extract the name from a ModelParameter reference.

details: The result is a string such as "Me", not a symbol with a global value. It is useful for labels, parameter overrides and exported code.
Names alone do not distinguish different model scopes. Retain the original ModelParameter when substituting in an amplitude.

examples.description: Read a declared parameter name.
List the names that resolved to numerical parameter values.

name: ModelParameterRules
summary: Resolve model parameters numerically without changing the symbolic amplitude or global session.

syntaxes.description: Resolve model variables and supported dependent functions.
Apply local overrides keyed by ModelParameter references or string names.

details: The default overrides are Automatic. Model variables and resolvable function dependencies are evaluated locally and returned as ordinary replacement rules.
A cyclic dependency, unknown external function or unresolved parameter is omitted rather than guessed. Unrelated parameters that can be resolved remain in the returned rules.
String overrides are convenient for user code, for example {"Me" -> 1, "EE" -> 1}. Typed parameter keys are useful when working with several models at once.
These replacements are appropriate for checks, fitting and exported numerical defaults. They do not overwrite the symbolic model list or assign names such as EE globally.

name: FactorizationPartitions
summary: Enumerate distinct complementary external-leg partitions for tree factorization.

syntaxes.description: Partition numbered external particles into two sides containing at least two external legs each.

details: External legs are tagged by their original positions, so two identical particles remain distinct numbered legs. A partition and its complement are included only once.
The output enumerates possible cuts before asking whether the supplied model supports a nonzero intermediate species and two nonzero lower-point amplitudes.
FactorizationAmplitudeChannels performs the model-dependent sewing. These partitions are combinatorial input and should not be summed as amplitudes.

examples.description: There are three distinct two-sided partitions at four points.
The five-point combinatorial partitions number ten.

name: LookupAmplitude
summary: Retrieve a complete model amplitude with its external labels reassigned.

syntaxes.description: Match particle names, multiply the stored factor, and relabel typed particle slots.

details: taggedParticles has entries {particleName, label}; labels may include Multiparticle for a sewn internal line. The four-entry spinIndices list supplies the indices used when an internal massive state must be explicit.

A lookup of ordinary external particles uses rightSide -> False as the third positional argument. The rightSide flag matters for internal-state index conventions when sewing opposite sides of a channel.
The matcher handles repeated particle names without replacing scalar coefficients, exponents or independent spin-index labels. If a complete amplitude is absent, the result is 0.
Use a model containing complete lower-point amplitudes. A product of bare vertex tensors is not a stored complete higher-point amplitude.

examples.description: Retrieve the QED positive-helicity three-point amplitude.
examples.input:
qedModel = ReadModel[modelDirectory, 2];
LookupAmplitude[{{"e", 1}, {"E", 2}, {"A.+", 3}}, qedModel, False, {i1, i2, i3, i4}]

examples.description: Missing model amplitudes give zero.
examples.input:
qedModel = ReadModel[modelDirectory, 2];
LookupAmplitude[{{"e", 1}, {"e", 2}, {"e", 3}}, qedModel, False, {i1, i2, i3, i4}]

name: FactorizationAmplitudeChannels
summary: Sew known lower-point amplitudes into the physical factorization channels.

syntaxes.description: Return the nonzero channel products for the specified all-ingoing process.

details: Each compact row contains the external masses, the cut Multiparticle label, the exchanged mass and the sewn lower-point product divided by z and the propagator denominator. The last entry is the expression; the preceding data identify its physical cut.

The model must supply the complete lower-point amplitudes needed on both sides. Missing amplitudes are zero. Four-point QED uses the three-point model, while five-point QED uses the model containing complete four-point amplitudes.
These are residue targets, not independent diagrams whose sum is a complete amplitude. Directly summing channels double counts overlapping pole information.
Keep the package's sewing convention. CheckAmplitudes converts the stored z convention and includes its required overall sewing sign once; do not add a manual sign to force agreement.

Fermion ordering is transported automatically from both lower amplitudes to one common particle/antiparticle reference order. The signs include internal fermion contraction orientation, the complete surviving fermion word across identical and distinct species, and the lower-to-full reference normalization. Boson and fermion channels use the same convention. Do not supply process-specific or cut-specific signs.

The fermion reference convention requires balanced Dirac particle/antiparticle pairs in each lower amplitude. Ambiguous self-conjugate fermion roles or unpaired fermion-number-violating rows return an UnsupportedFermionSewing failure rather than an assumed sign.

A channel may contain reference spinors that describe a continuation away from its cut. PrepareAmplitudes may simplify that continuation using only the selected channel shell. CompleteFactorization retains the original channel targets when preparation reports are supplied.
A FeynmanModel contains off-shell vertices, not the complete on-shell lower amplitudes required here, and is rejected as factorization input.

name: CreateDiagrams
summary: Generate tree diagrams from a supplied constructive or Feynman model.

syntaxes.description: Generate trees for an ordered all-ingoing external particle list.
Use the equivalent separate-particle argument form.

details: The external list determines particle labels 1, 2, and so on. Use the model's literal names, including massless helicity suffixes such as A.+ and A.-.
For constructive photon or gluon internal lines, one generic internal line represents both helicities. The graph count is not doubled for each internal helicity.

Each tree is an association containing graph and particle data, propagators, vertex information and index maps. Pass the resulting list to CreateArrowDiagrams for display or diagramAmplitudes for expressions.

Constructive and Feynman models follow their own amplitude rules. Feynman internal propagators and numerators remain off shell; constructive numerator preparation can use explicitly declared diagram-local shell conditions.
Use the model containing the intended vertices for diagram generation. A complete higher-point amplitude included for factorization is not automatically a new independent interaction in the theory.
Fewer than three external legs or unsupported particle names produce no generated diagrams.

name: CreateArrowDiagram
summary: Draw one generated tree with external labels and directed particle lines.

syntaxes.description: Draw one diagram returned by CreateDiagrams.
Optionally display the vertex and propagator expressions.

details: The input is one diagram association, not the list returned by CreateDiagrams. Use CreateArrowDiagrams to draw a whole process.
The string options "ShowVertexExpressions" and "ShowPropagatorExpressions" default to False. Enable them when inspecting how model vertices and internal lines are assigned.
Displaying a diagram does not derive or validate its amplitude. Use diagramAmplitudes and the construction/checking tools for that workflow.

name: CreateArrowDiagrams
summary: Draw the generated trees for a complete process.

syntaxes.description: Draw a list returned by CreateDiagrams.
Apply diagram display options to every tree.

details: Use this function to inspect all orderings and exchanged particles before working with expressions. External labels follow the input process order.

name: diagramAmplitude
summary: Evaluate the expression associated with one generated diagram.

syntaxes.description: Return one diagram's bare amplitude expression.

details: This lower-level singular function returns only the expression. For a process, use diagramAmplitudes, which retains each diagram's mass rules with its expression.
Constructive evaluation combines internal photon or gluon helicities and expands external x factors. Known mass replacements are applied before return.
Feynman evaluation retains ordered Dirac chains, Lorentz and color tensors, and off-shell internal lines. Convert Feynman tensors through the dedicated Feynman tools or preparation workflow.
A single diagram generally is neither reference independent nor a complete amplitude. Its simplification may need completion after diagrams are combined.

examples.description: Inspect the first constructive diagram expression.
Prefer the mass-rule pair when continuing to preparation.

name: diagramAmplitudes
summary: Evaluate every tree while retaining its separate mass and internal-cut declarations.

syntaxes.description: Return {{massRules, expression}, ...} for the generated diagrams.

details: The first entry of each pair declares external masses and, for constructive diagrams, the internal channel masses belonging to that diagram. The second entry is the expression with known mass replacements already applied.
Keep each diagram's conditions separate. Conditions from different constructive diagrams are not simultaneous shell assumptions for the complete sum.
Feynman diagram pairs contain external mass declarations without internal on-shell assumptions. Their exact propagators remain off shell.
External x factors are already expanded. Use PrepareAmplitudes next rather than manually repeating the old x-factor replacement step.
Total[Last /@ amplitudes] extracts the bare sum, but loses useful process and preparation provenance. Detailed preparation reports retain discarded terms for later completion.

name: DiagramAmplitudeRecords
summary: Retain explicit diagram expressions, physical propagators and numerator assumptions for diagnostics.

syntaxes.description: Build a record for each generated diagram without adding an automatic shell reduction.
Apply a supplied pair-preserving simplification and record any declared shell usage.

details: Each record contains "OriginalExpression", "Expression", "OriginalNumerator", "Numerator", "MassRules", "ExternalMassRules", "PhysicalPropagators" and the physical denominator. This is an inspection format rather than the normal user amplitude output.

The option "SimplificationFunction" defaults to Identity and receives {massRules, expression}. It must return that form with exactly the same mass rules. Propagator objects are protected during the transformation.

"NumeratorOnShellChannels" records any internal conditions used by the supplied transformation; merely declaring them does not apply them. "DenominatorsKeptOffShell" distinguishes numerator simplification from a residue restriction.
For routine bounded simplification and completion, PrepareAmplitudes with "ReturnDetails" -> True is the richer workflow because it retains discarded remainders and selected reference choices.

name: ExpandXFactors
summary: Apply the retained x-factor identities and external reference-spinor expansion.

syntaxes.description: Apply the supported x-factor rewrites for labels 1 through particleCount.

details: This helper includes older paired x-factor identities and an external-line replacement when exactly one external label is missing from the x-factor labels. That missing label identifies the external massless line.
The replacement introduces reference spinors. PrepareAmplitudes can choose their explicit forms through "PolePreference".

diagramAmplitudes already expands external x factors, so most modern calculations do not need a manual call. This helper is not a promise to eliminate every arbitrary x-factor structure at any multiplicity.

summary: Evaluate an older three-point vertex or a selected four-point exchange.

syntaxes.description: Match one three-point constructive amplitude.

details: This historical helper supports a three-particle vertex and a four-particle exchange. It is not the general tree generator for higher multiplicity.
The selected channel identifies which two of the four external particles meet on one side. The internal particle name must be present in the supplied particle table.
Use CreateDiagrams followed by diagramAmplitudes for new calculations. That route handles generic internal photon/gluon helicities, external x factors and per-diagram mass-rule pairs consistently.
The historical helper can return zero when no matching vertex or exchange exists and may print a diagnostic for unrecognized names. A zero here is not a full-process physical validation.

name: SimplifyFactorizationChannels
summary: Apply the historical spinor simplifier separately to compact channel rows.

syntaxes.description: Retain each channel row and simplify its last expression using its selected cut.

details: This historical helper builds external mass rules from each row and treats only that row's selected internal line as on shell. It then calls SimplifySpinorProducts with the corresponding momenta and mass replacements.
Simplifying on a cut preserves that channel residue while changing the continuation away from the cut. Do not combine the shell assumptions of several different rows.

PrepareAmplitudes is the preferred modern interface. It accepts the same compact rows, provides bounded effort and reference choices, and can preserve discarded remainders and original targets with "ReturnDetails" -> True.

name: SumResiduesAlt
summary: Sum the two finite-pole residues in a previously shifted channel representation.

syntaxes.description: Cancel removable factors and evaluate the zPlus and zMinus poles of each shifted channel.

details: This low-level historical ALT helper expects channel rows whose final expressions already contain the correct shifted rational dependence on z and the cut-specific zPlus and zMinus roots.
It cancels the pole factor before substituting the corresponding root and returns minus the sum of both residues over all supplied rows. This ordering avoids evaluating an uncanceled 0/0.
The helper does not generate the shift, determine its validity at infinity or repair missing boundary data. It is distinct from PhysicalPoleResidue, which verifies physical cut kinematics.
For the current diagram-and-factorization workflow, use CompleteFactorization and CheckAmplitudes instead of interpreting an arbitrary sum of channel products as the final amplitude.

name: PhysicalPoleResidue
summary: Extract a single- or compatible multiple-pole coefficient with explicit kinematic scope.

syntaxes.description: Extract the coefficient at one declared physical pole.
Extract a compatible multiple-pole coefficient.
Restrict the complete expression on a coherent physical cut chart.

details: The channel input is a normalized association or a list of such associations describing "Cut", "ExternalLegs", "Mass" and the matching propagator. DiagramAmplitudeRecords exposes suitable "PhysicalPropagators" records.

With "KinematicMap" -> Automatic, the result has "Status" -> "FORMAL". "StructuralCoefficient" treats PropDen as an opaque pole variable and does not prove that spinor numerators have the required physical residue.

A map is called as map[expression, channels, poleVariables]. It must evaluate spinors, momenta and denominators consistently while preserving external shells, momentum conservation and the selected cut coordinates without imposing unrelated cuts.

With a valid chart the physical result is stored in "PhysicalResidue". "KinematicKind" distinguishes numerical sample charts from symbolic charts. A sampled PASS is evidence on that chart, not an identity for all kinematics.

The full rational expression is canceled before cut substitution. A surviving higher-order pole, invalid chart or timeout returns UNRESOLVED rather than silently substituting into a singular denominator.
The default "StructuralCoefficient" -> True also computes the optional formal coefficient. False can save that extra symbolic work when the physical chart calculation is the intended result.
Physical residue extraction does not inherit a collection of internal numerator-shell assumptions from diagrams. The chosen cut is imposed through the chart.

examples.description: Extract a formal coefficient using a real diagram's cut record.
The same formal extraction does not claim physical cut validation.

name: CheckAmplitudes
summary: Check physical residues, apparent spurious poles, high-energy growth and reference dependence.

syntaxes.description: Run the combined checks and return a compact status table.
Check the sum while retaining external mass information.
Retain samples, differences, diagnostics and the run seed.

details: The first argument may be a bare expression, one {externalMassRules, expression} pair or a list of diagram-style pairs. The supplied compact FactorizationAmplitudeChannels rows identify the physical poles and expected lower-point products.

Physical residue comparisons include the package's fixed sewing conversion once. "Opp Sign" diagnoses a result that matches only after a global minus sign; it does not change the amplitude or fit a sign.

Apparent denominator factors outside the known physical channels are discovered automatically and checked for spurious singularities. Finite approach tests are numerical evidence, not a replacement for an analytic cancellation when one is practical.

High-energy checks scale conserved external kinematics with fixed masses and inspect all sampled spin assignments. The automatic renormalizable tree target is E^(4-n); "HighEnergyBound" can state another theory's expected bound.

Large reference-free typed expressions may certify a conservative upper bound from external-spinor and momentum degrees. Every massive spin-basis column and each propagator's nonzero leading invariant are checked on the actual conserved high-energy chart. The report records ObservedPowerUpperBound and leaves ObservedPower missing because no leading Laurent coefficient was measured.

Unsupported structures, explicit references, hidden spinor denominators, degenerate leading invariants or an upper bound above the target retain the exact Laurent fallback. Multiparticle propagator growth does not establish model membership: the physical and spurious-pole checks remain separate and unchanged. Internal virtualities are never set on shell for either energy method.

Reference tests vary explicit external Xi spinors on conserved kinematics. If none remain, the report establishes absence of explicit Xi dependence; that alone is not a separate analytic Ward-identity proof.
Supply "FeynmanAmplitudes" and the matching "FeynmanModel" for an independent full-amplitude comparison at ordinary off-cut kinematics.

The full Feynman comparison checks every coherent massive-spin monomial from both sums. Scalar coefficients are reduced separately so a large spin tensor does not require one multivariate polynomial cancellation. Both exact differences and opposite-sign diagnostics are retained; the numerical zero-test convention and requested sample count are unchanged.

Off-cut Feynman sampling first tries bounded deterministic rational geometries. If an accidental physical pole invalidates one geometry, a fresh geometry is tried before the real center-of-mass fallback. Acceptance uses only external shells, conservation, spinor-basis consistency and nonzero physical propagators, never amplitude agreement. Details retain rejected cuts and geometry attempts.

Numerical external spinor bases use known masses and stable real direction components to avoid cancellation in highly boosted or nearly axial configurations. Exact and complex chart formulas retain their analytic branches; internal virtualities are not assigned an external mass shell.

Default numerical parameter values come from the model. "ParameterRules" locally overrides selected values without changing the symbolic amplitude. "RandomSeed" -> Automatic chooses a time-based seed once; provide an integer to replay samples.

The ordinary table is deliberately short. "Output" -> "Residues" shows calculated and expected sampled values, "Summary" counts statuses, and "Details" retains the complete report. Other focused outputs include "HighEnergy", "References" and "Feynman".

PASS, Opp Sign, FAIL and UNRESOLVED describe the performed tests. They do not establish a generic symbolic reconstruction or uniqueness theorem. Do not interpret a disabled or unresolved test as a pass.
Independent checks can use "Parallelization" -> Automatic and "MaxKernels" -> Automatic. Set False or 1 for serial execution; effective speed depends on expression size and worker setup cost.

name: PrepareAmplitudes
summary: Simplify diagram pairs or factorization rows while retaining their physical assumptions.

syntaxes.description: Prepare a mass-rule pair, a list of diagram pairs or compact factorization-channel rows.
Choose and simplify a bounded set of allowed reference-spinor assignments.
Retain original inputs, selected references, discarded remainders and preparation diagnostics.

details: The ordinary result retains the input format with each expression replaced by its prepared form. "Output" -> "Expression" returns the sum instead. The detailed report is optional so routine use does not expose implementation data.

Preparation applies ReduceSpinContractions, chooses reference spinors, then applies ReduceSpinorProducts and bounded improving identities. Momentum conservation is used with the known external leg set rather than added as an unconditional chain rewrite.

A bounded numerator pass can factor existing spectator spinor chains to expose small Schouten and external Dirac identities. Each complete inverse-factor product stays separate, inverse factors are protected, and only a strict improvement of the complete expression is retained. Unsupported sectors and interrupted trials keep their last completed expression.

A further bounded ordinary-identity pass handles supported numerators with six distinct external spinor slots and at most one momentum insertion per monomial. It searches Schouten, external Dirac and, when enabled, declared total-momentum-conservation identities. A numerical optimization only proposes a sparse form: exact rational identity coefficients and a zero algebraic replay residual are required before accepting it. Denominators and internal virtualities are unchanged; this does not prove a global minimum.

For completed external amplitudes, ordinary external pair definitions can first cancel apparent repeated propagators without internal-shell conditions. A bounded shared-matrix identity can then expose one or two literal positive spectator chain factors and smaller six-spinor coefficients. A two-factor route removes only witnessed polynomial factors, preserves each original fraction, and requires exact identity replay after lifting the spectators back. Inverse factors are unchanged by that cofactor route. Only complete improving checkpoints are returned. This final-amplitude route leaves the diagram/channel source partitions used by completion unchanged.

For completed amplitudes, the original-fraction alternative can continue from each strictly improving ordinary-identity checkpoint. Short searches share the remaining preparation clock rather than restarting contraction expansion. It stops when no better checkpoint is found, its finite pass limit is reached, or the existing time allowance expires. The detailed OriginalFractionSpinorIdentities reduction records CheckpointIterations, StopReason and the complete ordinary identity route. This is a bounded multistep search, not a proof of minimality.

Constructive internal-shell simplification acts on each item's numerator using only that item's mass declarations. Physical PropDen objects stay off shell. A channel row declares only its own cut; completed external-mass pairs declare no internal cut.

ReduceSpinorProducts itself applies the ordinary external-shell identities. The additional diagram-local internal-shell reductions belong to preparation and may be disabled with "InternalOnShell" -> False.

"PolePreference" -> "AllPhysical" compares momentum-insertion references that introduce physical denominator channels outside the current diagram's cuts. "AllSpurious" compares references built from other eligible massless particles. "Mixed" permits both; Automatic compares admissible choices within a bounded budget.

"Cyclic" and "ReverseCyclic" retain fixed massless reference cycles. "Xi" uses a common reference, "IndependentXi" keeps separate generic references, and None leaves the references unchanged. An unavailable requested choice is reported rather than silently declared successful.

The search ranks completed trials by expression complexity and respects bounded time and candidate limits. Measuring a completed candidate has a separate bounded allowance from distributing identity trials, so a moderately large but cheaply measured expression is still ranked by its spinor complexity. A leaf-count fallback is not compared against a weighted-complexity score. The search does not prove a global minimum. Automatic resource settings scale to the process; user values remain authoritative.

The detailed output retains original expressions and discarded remainders so CompleteFactorization can first reuse information lost in aggressive preparation. Pass the report itself when preserving that information matters.
Feynman inputs use coherent external references for the whole diagram sum and never declare internal lines on shell. The reference assignment is fixed before independent items are sent to workers.

"Parallelization" and "MaxKernels" default to Automatic. Items are independent jobs, input order is retained, and user progress runs on the main kernel. "MaxSteps" -> 0 disables the bounded identity search but keeps deterministic algebraic and permitted scalar-shell reductions.

The same interface can simplify a completed amplitude returned as {externalMassRules, expression}; with no internal mass declarations it uses only ordinary identities. It never adds factorization corrections or model interactions.

name: CompleteFactorization
summary: Repair physical residue deficits with a bounded simultaneous correction fit.

syntaxes.description: Fit corrections against all known physical channels simultaneously.
Start from prepared inputs while retaining discarded expressions and original residue targets.
Keep the candidate, affine freedom, correction directions and validation diagnostics.

details: The function starts with the supplied amplitude, compares every physical residue with its lower-point target and solves for correction coefficients together. It does not naively add the channel products, which overlap on multiple poles.

When MaxCorrectionTerms is Automatic, an already built and projected exchange-symmetry correction union can be admitted within the automatic ceiling without rebuilding its sources. CapChanges records the effective increase and preserved direction count. Later source builders use the construction allowance implied by that effective cap, recorded as SourceConstructionLimit. This never extends TimeConstraint, truncates columns or changes residue and affine-family validation. Explicit numerical caps and supplied correction bases retain their limits.

Preparation details provide simplified expressions, original expressions and discarded remainders. These are tried before broader channel-continuation directions, preserving useful diagram information without making a hard-coded process formula.

Before admitting a source to a simple-physical-pole proposal, a bounded ordinary external pair-virtuality cancellation can remove apparent repeated propagators. For a massless leg k and an external leg p of mass m, PropDen[p+k,m] equals 2 p.k without putting the internal line on shell. Newly exposed regular quotients stay correlated with their complete source under one coefficient, including a wholly regular quotient; their coefficients are not claimed to be fixed by residues. Already-explicit regular input is fixed separately and removed per input record before source normalization. Uncanceled positive numerator virtualities are restored as momentum products. Genuine higher-order poles still fail the existing simple-pole admission guard.

For sufficiently large coherent-spin systems, a preliminary proposal keeps related terms of existing prepared sources and their retained remainders together, grouped by momentum-insertion degree. It fits that complete proposal against every original channel before attempting wider continuation spaces. The first proposal keeps prepared whole sources in their physical form and preserves the supplied discarded remainders through grouping and exchange projection; eligibility is checked on canonical copies. Rewriting those remainders is deferred to the fit so early rewrites do not accidentally favor a more complicated representative. A normalized source proposal remains a fallback within the same clock and explicit limits. Neither changes the physical targets.

Residue sampling may skip the numerator evaluation of a coordinate that is structurally regular at the selected cut, after verifying every other inverse factor is finite and nonzero on that same exact chart. The coordinate remains in the system. Hidden spinor inverses, coincident poles and unsupported or custom charts use the full residue evaluator.

The correction space is finite and bounded. Alternative reference continuations, input reweighting and retained terms can supply additional directions. Failure to span a deficit is reported honestly; the function does not invent unknown lower amplitudes or arbitrary interactions.
The ordinary successful output is {externalMassRules, expression}. No internal shell declaration survives for the complete amplitude. It can be passed to PrepareAmplitudes or CompleteHighEnergy.

"Output" -> "Expression" gives the bare expression. "ReturnDetails" -> True or "Output" -> "Details" exposes the fit, correction, channel continuations, refinement history and validation. Request details when CompleteHighEnergy must retain residue-preserving affine freedom.

"PolePreference" biases representation and continuation choices. AllPhysical favors physical-only inverse factors; it is not permission to return an unchecked expression or a proof that the result is globally simplest.

Identical boson and fermion permutations are inferred from ordered external particle identities and the model's twice-spin declarations. Equal masses alone cannot identify the species. Supply "ExternalParticles" when a bare input has lost the ordered process metadata.

Numerical fitting uses locally resolved model parameters. A time-based seed is chosen once for Automatic; an integer replays the sampling. Independent validation and failed-sample refinement guard against a fit that happens to match its training points.

A large inconsistent exact system may be rejected by a verified left-null contradiction certificate instead of computing its full affine solution. Every original coefficient column and the nonzero constant residual are checked exactly. If no exact matrix rank was computed, details report Rank as Missing and give RankLowerBound separately; successful and underdetermined solutions retain their exact-rank and full-family checks.

Automatic effort settings bound runtime and correction size. An unresolved result normally returns a concise Failure rather than an unchecked amplitude. Detailed reports distinguish complete, incomplete and underdetermined cases.

Physical residue agreement leaves any genuine pole-free or residue-preserving freedom for CompleteHighEnergy and other stated physical constraints. No universal uniqueness claim follows from sampled residues alone.

Exact integer, rational and Gaussian-rational coefficients have exact zero decisions without a numerical tolerance. Other algebraic coefficients retain algebraic normalization; approximate or unresolved symbolic values are not silently accepted as exact proof.

name: CompleteHighEnergy
summary: Fit retained residue-preserving freedom to high-energy, spurious-pole and reference constraints.

syntaxes.description: Constrain a completed amplitude and its retained correction freedom.
Inspect the fit equations, affine family and independent validation.

details: Pass detailed CompleteFactorization output when its remaining affine directions are needed. Alternatively supply a justified explicit "CorrectionBasis". Automatic uses retained information and does not create an unrestricted contact-operator ansatz.

The fitted directions must preserve the known physical residues. High-energy scaling, apparent spurious singularities and explicit reference dependence are tested together, and the candidate is validated again against the original channels.

The default high-energy target is the renormalizable tree bound E^(4-n), with masses held fixed. "HighEnergyBound" can express another stated bound; it is a physical input rather than an arbitrary fitting preference.

Independent high-energy validation may use a conservative all-spin upper-bound certificate for supported large expressions. Such a report records ObservedPowerUpperBound and leaves ObservedPower missing; it does not claim a measured leading Laurent power. Unsupported or inconclusive certificates retain the ordinary exact Laurent comparison.

When an exact Laurent expansion is needed, large coherent-spin polynomials can first be separated into all of their scalar coefficients without expanding the kinematic coefficient field. Every coefficient is expanded and reassembled exactly; no spin components or small coefficients are sampled away. Independent high-energy samples share one deadline and can run on separate workers. Large retained families can use the same exact coefficient separation to build fitting equations; correction unknowns are reassembled before extracting equations, so a condition such as x+y=0 retains its coupled freedom.

If Series assumes an exact numeric radical coefficient is zero, that assumption is accepted only after an exact algebraic zero certificate. A tiny genuine nonzero value, an unproved assumption, another warning or an insufficient expansion order keeps the result unresolved or on its original fallback. Details retain these certificates.

A successful ordinary result keeps the {externalMassRules, expression} form. There are no new internal on-shell conditions on this combined amplitude, so it may be simplified again with PrepareAmplitudes.

"Output" -> "Details" retains the candidate, equations, fitted family and validation. A timeout, unsupported direction space or unresolved free coefficient is not silently assigned an arbitrary value.

Exact identity proofs receive an allowance based on both the number and the size of retained affine directions. A small family containing a large expression can therefore receive more proof time, still within the stage's TimeConstraint. Details records FamilyIdentityProofBudget, including DirectionCount, LargestDirectionLeafCount and AllocatedSeconds. This changes resource allocation only: an unproved direction is retained, and genuine undetermined interactions are not discarded.

For a large coherent-spin direction whose original symbolic proof is expensive, a bounded retry factors numerator spectators and compacts each physical-pole group using ordinary identities. It keeps the original direction and the reduction route, then requires the existing generic symbolic external-kinematics certificate on the compact expression. It does not use internal shells or sampled zeros as a proof; an unfinished attempt retains the direction.

A late serial fallback can prove supported identities on a dense symbolic external rest/null chart using complete exact Laurent-polynomial arithmetic. It chooses angle or square null-spinor axes from the expression, then verifies external shells, conservation, spinor reconstruction, typed homogeneity, coefficient coverage and a nonzero off-cut denominator domain. Unit normalization requires exact mass/coupling witnesses; it is not a numerical phase-space test. The optional local runtime uses Python 3, a C++17 compiler and Boost headers. Missing tools, unsupported structure or any resource limit preserve the unproved direction. All preparation, compilation and evaluation remain inside the existing shared deadline.
Use model-local "ParameterRules" only for numerical sampling. An explicit "RandomSeed" replays the run; Automatic records a newly chosen time-based seed in details.
This stage cannot establish an unknown interaction merely because it would improve high-energy behavior. The model and supplied direction space determine what is being solved.

name: ConstructAmplitude
summary: Construct, complete, simplify and validate an amplitude from its process and two models.

syntaxes.description: Run the full workflow and return the validated bare expression.
Retain the external mass rules with the expression.
Retain stage outputs, timings, checks and the chosen run seed.

details: The process is an ordered all-ingoing particle list. Use the diagram model for vertices and a factorization model containing the complete lower-point amplitudes. Four-point QED can use the three-point model for both roles; five-point QED needs the model containing complete four-point amplitudes for factorization.

The stages generate and prepare diagram amplitudes, generate and prepare channel continuations, complete physical factorization, complete high-energy behavior, simplify the completed amplitude with ordinary external identities, and run the final checks.
Original residue targets, discarded preparation remainders and residual affine freedom are retained between stages. Final preparation never puts a combined amplitude's internal propagators on shell.

A bare expression is returned only when every required final check passes. An opposite-sign, failed, unresolved or underdetermined case remains a Failure or detailed diagnostic report, not an alleged validated result.

The defaults choose bounded resources automatically according to multiplicity and workload. Routine examples need only the three main arguments. "TimeConstraint", "Parallelization" and "MaxKernels" can override the automatic choices.
"PolePreference" controls reference choices and representation preferences through preparation and completion. For example, "AllPhysical" asks the workflow to favor physical-only denominator forms.

Progress shows the current stage, its elapsed time and the total elapsed time. The final printed report shows time, the chosen seed and test results before the expression. "ProgressReporting" -> False and "PrintReport" -> False suppress these displays.
"RandomSeed" -> Automatic chooses one time-based run seed from which stage seeds are derived. Give an integer to reproduce sampling and inspect "Details" to preserve the actual seed.
"FeynmanModel" can supply an independent off-shell benchmark. It is a separate semantic input and cannot be guessed from the constructive factorization model.

Advanced stage-specific options are supplied in "PreparationOptions", "ChannelPreparationOptions", "FactorizationOptions", "HighEnergyOptions", "FinalPreparationOptions", "CheckOptions" and "FeynmanPreparationOptions". These are optional refinements, not required boilerplate.

Identical boson and fermion symmetry is inferred from the process identities and the model. Fixed photon helicities are distinct process choices; amplitudes differing by those choices can later be exported together with WriteSPINASProcess.
